To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
primary cultures of mucus cells can be established from elutriation-purified gastric epithelial cells and that these cells respond to a number of growth factors.
we developed a novel method for the enrichment of gastric mucus-producing cells from the rat gastric mucosa by counterflow elution, and established a primary culture of mucus-producing cells.
we established a mucus-producing cell line from elutriation-enriched primary rat gastric mucosal epithelial cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of primary epithelial cells from elutriation of rat gastric mucosal tissue.
the establishment of primary cell cultures from rat gastric epithelial cells.
the development and application of a new cell culture system of gastric mucosal cells that may be suitable for the study of the mechanisms of gastric mucosal cell proliferation and differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cells in the medium-sized cell fraction are not parietal, chief, or ECL cells, but are mucus-producing cells that can be grown in culture.
the cell lines described here represent the first example of an in vitro culture of mucus cells from the stomach.
the gastric mucosal cell culture system described here is a valuable model with which to study mucus cell biology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the primary cell culture of mucus-producing cells is a useful in vitro system for studying the function of gastric surface mucous cells and their interaction with other cells.
we established a gastric mucosa cell culture system from rat stomach.
gastric mucus cells can be successfully cultured and that the culture system is a useful model to elucidate the mechanism of mucus secretion.

the mucus-producing cells in our cultures were derived from the surface epithelium and not from the glands.
